subject: StableLink: Executive war-room & customer status — critical throughput regression
messages:
From: Judy Park <judy.park@stablelink.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: StableLink Platform Team <ops@stablelink.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Dec 2028 08:05:12 -0800
Subject: Immediate: 40% throughput drop + rising 5xx — impacting checkouts

Hi Sean / Monica,

We started seeing a sharp throughput degradation this morning around 07:50 PST. Token throughput for our checkout flow is ~60% of normal and 5xx errors have climbed from 0.2% to ~6% (user-facing failures). Latency p95 has increased from ~220ms to ~1.2s. This is impacting dozens of merchant checkouts per minute.

We've already validated it isn't a client-side spike (request rate steady). Attached are a short stack trace and sample request ids. Can you confirm receipt and advise next steps? We need an ETA on mitigation or a controlled rollback.

Attachments: server-logs-20281207.zip (partial logs), request-samples.txt

— Judy Park
Head of Site Reliability, StableLink
judy.park@stablelink.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Judy Park <judy.park@stablelink.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Dec 2028 08:12:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Immediate: 40% throughput drop + rising 5xx — impacting checkouts

Acknowledged. Opening an exec war-room now. Monica, take lead on customer comms and timeline. Karthik & Grace, please triage runtime metrics and kernel selection + batching config. Marissa, coordinate on rollbacks/fallback model variants. David, loop in infra (cloud) and check for noisy nodes or autoscale flaps.

I'll get an executive summary to StableLink in the next 30 minutes and ping the AWS AMI if we need provider-side assistance.

Date: Thu, 7 Dec 2028 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Immediate: 40% throughput drop + rising 5xx — impacting checkouts

Judy — thanks for the logs. Quick status: we've confirmed a correlated increase in KV cache misses and unusually high prefill time on two serving shards. Preliminary root cause hypothesis: degraded NVLink performance on a subset of hosts + a recently deployed kernel change that sensitizes certain sequence-length distributions.

Action plan (next 60 mins):
- War-room active: engineering + infra + customer comms
- Roll forward a compatibility patch to the batcher that reduces aggressive packing (Karthik & Grace, in-flight)
- Prepare a controlled failover to fallback model variant with lower memory footprint (Marissa)
- Upload logs and timeline to shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/StableLink/incident-20281207

ETA for measurable improvement: 30–45 mins for rollback/fallback; 60–90 mins for full stability. We'll update every 20 mins.

Attachment: timeline-runbook-v2.pdf

— Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Judy Park <judy.park@stablelink.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Dec 2028 09:01:47 -0800
Subject: Re: Immediate: 40% throughput drop + rising 5xx — impacting checkouts

Quick technical update from runtime triage:
- Confirmed NVLink errors + elevated kernel queue latency on hosts rack-14 (3 nodes). Cloud provider telemetry shows PCIe resets coincident with the spike.
- Rolling a temporary batching change now: disable large-minded packing; target smaller batches for checkout route only. Expected to reduce prefill latency and KV pressure.
- Preparing a model fallback (quantized variant) staged to run on spare hosts — Marissa will trigger if packing change doesn't recover.

I'll monitor token-level error rates and kv cache hit ratio; will post metrics link in 10 mins.

— Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Judy Park <judy.park@stablelink.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 7 Dec 2028 12:34:00 -0800
Subject: StableLink incident update — mitigation in place, next steps

Judy — update for your execs and ops: first, thank you for the quick signals and logs. Summary as of 12:34 PST:

- Root cause: NVLink instability on 3 dedicated serving hosts causing elevated kernel queue latency and increased KV cache misses. Kernel packing change exacerbated the effect for your sequence-length distribution.
- Mitigation completed: reverted the packing change (08:55), applied targeted smaller-batch policy to checkout route (09:05), and failed over traffic off the three problematic hosts to the quantized fallback variant (09:40).

Impact and status:
- Throughput recovered to ~98% of baseline.
- 5xx errors reduced to 0.25% and trending down.
- p95 latency back to ~240ms.

Next steps:
1) Provider remediation: we requested host replacement from AWS AMI; they initiated ECC checks and host swap for rack-14.
2) Post-incident: full RCA and remediation plan to be delivered by EOD tomorrow.
3) Preventive: reverting kernel packing change across canary groups until we ship a sequence-aware packing patch.

Attachments: server-logs-20281207.zip (redacted), timeline-runbook-v2.pdf
Related: Jira SLINK-4983 created for follow-ups.

We will remain in a monitoring posture and will send a formal RCA tomorrow. Please advise if you'd like a short exec briefing (15–20 mins) — Sean can join.

— Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
